stem: The wavelength of the visible spectrum is in the range :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: It is difficult to define an exact boundary of the visible spectrum (light), because it depends on factors such as a person’s age, eyesight, distance of the light source, intensity, etc. Generally, its range is considered to be 320 nanometers to 860 nanometers. [In Angstrom (Å), this will be 3200 Å to 8600 Å.] The US space agency (NASA) has stated its range as 380 to 700 nanometers (nm). In the NCERT textbook, the range is written as 400 to 700 nanometers. Therefore, as per the options given in the question, candidates can choose the nearest correct answer within this range.

stem: The amount of light flux produced by an isotropic source of 2 candela is -

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The SI unit of luminous flux (light flux) is lumen. Luminous flux is denoted by F. F = 4πI = 4π × 2 = 8π lumen Thus, the luminous flux produced by an isotropic source of 2 candela is 8π lumen.

stem: Though water is transparent to visible light, it is not possible to see distant objects in fog which consists of fine drops of water. This is so because :

options.text: fine drops of water are opaque to visible light

stem: How does the white light produce in the tube?

options.label: a
options.text: By heating up the copper wire

expl: In a fluorescent tube, mercury vapor at low pressure is present. When electric current is passed through the filaments at the ends, the mercury vapor emits invisible ultraviolet rays. These ultraviolet rays strike the fluorescent coating (phosphor layer) on the inner surface of the tube, which then emits visible light.

stem: On what does the light in a tube light depend?
expl: In a tube light, tungsten filaments are present at both ends of the glass tube, and mercury vapor at low pressure is filled inside. When the switch is turned on, electrons are emitted from the tungsten filament and ionize mercury vapor molecules, producing a luminous discharge. Some of the emitted radiation has very small wavelengths and is not visible to us. To convert this invisible radiation into visible light, the inner surface of the tube is coated with a fluorescent (phosphor) substance, which converts invisible radiation into visible light.

stem: Which of the following does not change when light travels from one medium to another?

options.label: e

expl: When a light wave goes from air to glass, or from one medium to another, its frequency remains the same, but its wavelength and speed change.

stem: Sky is blue because –

options.label: a
options.text: Blue color in the sunlight is more than other colors

options.label: b
options.text: Short waves are scattered more than long waves by atmosphere

options.label: c
options.text: Blue color is more absorbing to eyes

options.label: d
options.text: Atmosphere absorbs long wavelength more than short wavelength

expl: The sky appears blue because Rayleigh scattering of the Sun’s white light occurs in the atmosphere. Small atmospheric particles scatter shorter wavelengths more than longer wavelengths. Since blue and violet have shorter wavelengths, they scatter more; however, violet is less visible to us, so mainly the scattered blue light reaches our eyes. Therefore, the sky looks blue.

stem: The vision defect 'nearsightedness' is known as.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The defect of short-sightedness is called Myopia (Myopia). A person suffering from this defect can see nearby objects easily, but cannot see distant objects. This problem occurs due to a decrease in the focal length of the eye lens, an increase in the curvature of the lens, and an increase in the power of the lens. To correct it, a concave lens (Concave Lens) of suitable focal length is used.

stem: If the power of a glass lens is +2 diopters, its focal length will be :
expl: The SI unit of lens power is m-1 (dioptre), denoted by the symbol D. If the focal length (f) is expressed in meters, then 1 D = 1 m-1. Thus, the lens whose focal length is 1 m has power of lense 1 D. The power of a converging (convex) lens is positive (+) and the power of a diverging (concave) lens is negative (–). Focal length (f) = 1 / Power of lense (D) = 1/2 = 0.5 meter or 50 cm

stem: The focal distance ofa plane mirror is:
expl: The focal length of a mirror is the distance between the pole and the principal focus. A plane mirror can be treated as a special case of a spherical mirror where the radius of curvature becomes infinite (∞). For a spherical mirror, f = R / 2 → ∞ / 2 = ∞ If R = ∞, then f = ∞. Therefore, the focal length of a plane mirror is considered infinite, and its optical power is zero.

stem: In a barber's shop, two plane mirrors are placed

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: A plane mirror is a thin, flat, smooth sheet of glass with a shiny silver coating on one side. The image formed by a plane mirror is virtual and erect. The image size is equal to the object size. The image of an object forms behind the mirror at the same distance as the object is placed in front of the mirror. In barber shops, plane mirrors are used and are kept parallel to each other.

stem: In big showrooms and departmental stores, the vigilance mirror used is a -

expl: A convex mirror is a spherical mirror in which reflection takes place from the convex surface. Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles to see the traffic coming from behind. They are also used as vigilance mirrors in large showrooms and departmental stores.

stem: Reading glasses are made from which type of lenses?
expl: Reading glasses are generally made from convex lenses. Such lenses are useful in hypermetropia (long-sightedness) and in age-related defective near vision called presbyopia. With increasing age, the power of accommodation of the human eye decreases. In most persons, the near point shifts farther away. Without corrective spectacles, they find it difficult to see nearby objects clearly and comfortably. This defect is called presbyopia. In hypermetropia also, a person cannot see nearby objects, but the reason is different—for example, the eyeball may be shorter than normal or the lens may have less focusing power, due to which the image forms behind the retina.
